title: HB 162 (110th General Assembly): As enacted, permits the sending of an absentee ballot to an address within a county, regardless of whether the voter requesting the absentee ballot possesses a commercial driver license or a valid transportation worker identification credential. - Amends TCA Title 2, Chapter 6.

(other) Section 1: replaces item (E) of the absentee application contents in 2-6-202(a)(3) with 'The address to mail the ballot outside the county, if applicable;'.
(other) Section 2: takes effect on becoming law.
(other) version: Draft 1486192 (2017-01-30): the one-item change to 2-6-202(a)(3)(E); no slot a-e content.
(other) version: Chaptered 1801742 (2017-04-19): the Public Chapter as signed is the Senate bill's chapter (SB 286, substituted for HB 162); same operative text as the Draft.
(other) note: The House bill itself was set aside ('Comp. SB subst.' 2017-04-03); the law is the Senate bill's Public Chapter 137 (signed 2017-04-17, effective 04/17/2017). No roll calls saved for HB 162. The saved chaptered text is a scan with garbled characters ('(aX3XE)') but reads as (a)(3)(E). The title says the change lets a ballot go to an address within the county regardless of driver license status; the saved text reads only as quoted. No ID or citizenship content.
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
